draft.title: Resolve an alias before reading a score
draft.statement: Implement lookup_alias_score(aliases, scores, alias, fallback). The aliases object maps alias strings to name strings; scores maps name strings to integer scores. Return the score for the name assigned to the requested alias. If the alias is absent, or its assigned name has no score, return fallback. A score stored under the original alias is irrelevant unless that string is also the assigned name. Empty strings are valid aliases and names, and zero and negative scores are valid. Match both keys exactly, with case sensitivity. Inputs are valid JSON: aliases contains only string values, scores only integer values (not booleans), alias is a string and fallback is an integer. Do not mutate either map. Return the integer result; do not print it.

constraints: Both flat maps have at most 1000 string keys; aliases has string values and scores has integer values excluding booleans.
Resolve exactly one alias mapping, then exactly one score lookup; do not recursively follow aliases.
The original alias is never an implicit name when its mapping is absent. Empty resolved strings remain valid keys.
Do not mutate either map. Return-value checks alone do not certify non-mutation.

rubric.criterion: Use the resolved alias value as the second lookup key; return caller fallback when either required mapping is absent, while preserving empty string targets, exact key identity, zero and negative scores.
rubric.family_rule: Fixed two-hop data dependency: a value retrieved from one flat map determines the key used in a second map. P01/S015 teach one-map membership/default lookup but not this dependency. Prior exposure to this chain or its solution still precludes a claim of unseen work.
rubric.limits: AI-reviewed content classification only. Finite cases do not establish learner independence, arbitrary nested/recursive lookup, non-mutation, complexity or mastery.

examples.explanation: The alias ace names Ada, whose stored score is 8.
The requested alias is absent, so use the caller fallback.

assistance_steps.content: There are two maps with different jobs. Check what information is available at each stage and what a missing entry means.
The value retrieved from aliases becomes the key used in scores. Stop with the fallback if the requested alias is absent; an empty resolved string can still be a valid key.
If the alias is absent, return fallback. Otherwise obtain its mapped name, then return that name's score if present or fallback if absent.
First guard `alias not in aliases`. After that guard, assign `name = aliases[alias]` and use name, not alias, for the final score/default lookup.
The complete implementation performs the guarded alias lookup before selecting a score with the caller fallback. Empty names and zero scores are valid values.

solution.explanation: The requested alias must exist before a name is available. Its stored string becomes the score lookup key, even when empty. The score lookup preserves zero and uses the caller fallback only for a missing name. Neither map is modified.
solution.expected_complexity: Two expected O(1) dictionary lookups and O(1) extra space; reviewed, not certified by finite tests.
